summary: This Part II of RankZeroOneBSD supplies the good odd Eisenstein-prime converse in Selmer coranks zero and one, its finite-Selmer form, and positive proportions of low-rank quadratic twists on the precisely admissible local family. The proof combines complementary twists, rational augmentation control and the parent’s Heegner index-square equality. CM rank-zero converses and Skinner’s irreducible branch retain their existing owners. All six layers are planned; the shared Cassels–Tate supplier endpoint is an explicit frontier, and no implementation is claimed.

declarations.provides: Over a number field, the set of elements of bounded logarithmic height is finite; the existing Northcott instances discharge the field-height hypothesis.
The finite-fiber x-coordinate comparison transfers Northcott from field height to point naive height; its bounded-height sets are finite.
For an elliptic affine Weierstrass model over a field with admissible absolute values and decidable equality, the pinned canonical height of every point is nonnegative.

Under the same field/ellipticity conditions and Northcott for canonical height, that height is zero exactly on points of finite additive order. The existing instances transfer Northcott from naive height.
The five-coefficient Weierstrass carrier over any ring; no replacement elliptic-curve carrier is introduced.
The exact discriminant polynomial used in both concrete computations.
The c₄ polynomial and hence the explicit j numerator.
The c₆ polynomial; for the nineteen-a3 model its value is8.
The typeclass asserting the discriminant is a unit.
The j-invariant using the inverse discriminant unit, with an IsElliptic instance.
Coefficientwise base change along a ring homomorphism.
The existing trace/norm-parameter twist by t,n with discriminant parameter t²−4n; it is not a one-parameter raw coefficient formula.
For any commutative ring, Δ(E.quadraticTwistOf t n)=(t²−4n)⁶Δ(E).

nodes.title: The fixed-isogeny converse hypotheses
nodes.statement: EisensteinConverseData(E,p,ι) records precisely the good odd prime, the actual rational cyclic degree-p isogeny and the local exclusion in the standing hypothesis. The character is the Galois action on ker ι, not an arbitrarily selected semisimple constituent. Reuse upstream isogeny, residual-character, reduction and conductor carriers; this is a Prop-valued hypothesis bundle, not a second elliptic-curve structure. Witness equality is inherited from proof irrelevance; no separate extensionality theorem is needed.
hypotheses: E/ℚ is a Weierstrass curve with IsElliptic, conductor N; p is prime, p>2 and p∤N; ι:E→E′ is a rational cyclic isogeny of degree p. Its actual kernel character φ:G_ℚ→𝔽_pˣ satisfies φ|G_p∉{1,ω}, with ω the mod-p cyclotomic character. The residual quotient character is ψ=ωφ⁻¹.
proofSteps: Bundle the existing predicates and kernel-character equality. Import the Weil-pairing identity φψ=ω. Retain the actual isogeny throughout twisting and duality.
acceptance: Good ordinarity and E(ℚ_p)[p]=0 are consequences supplied by BSD.7a; no irreducibility or parity condition on φ at infinity is added.

sources.locator: Introduction, Theorem E and standing hypotheses, pp. 517–521; Theorem 5.2.1, p. 574
sources.match: The good odd Eisenstein setting and the two excluded local characters are the exact scope of the converse.

uses.how: Fix the same kernel character for parity, auxiliary fields and the main-conjecture input.
Transport the actual isogeny and its character, retaining good reduction.

nodes.title: A Selmer group of dimension zero or one
nodes.statement: Under EisensteinConverseData, for r∈{0,1}, dim_𝔽p Sel_p(E/ℚ)=r implies corank_ℤp Sel_{p∞}(E/ℚ)=r. More precisely, E(ℚ)[p]=0 gives Sel_p≅Sel_{p∞}[p]; the latter dimension is corank Sel_{p∞}+2 dim_𝔽p M[p] for a finite p-group M from the paired elementary divisors of the nondivisible Sha part. No finiteness of the whole Sha group is assumed.
hypotheses: E/ℚ is a Weierstrass curve with IsElliptic, conductor N; p is prime, p>2 and p∤N; ι:E→E′ is a rational cyclic isogeny of degree p. Its actual kernel character φ:G_ℚ→𝔽_pˣ satisfies φ|G_p∉{1,ω}, with ω the mod-p cyclotomic character. The residual quotient character is ψ=ωφ⁻¹.
Use cofinite generation of Sel_{p∞} and finite-level Kummer exactness. The requested Cassels–Tate result is on Sha modulo its maximal divisible subgroup.
proofSteps: Use the coefficient sequence E[p]→E[p∞] and rational p-torsion vanishing to identify the p-torsion Selmer group.

Apply the shared pairing with its divisible kernels to the finite nondivisible p-primary Sha quotient. Its paired elementary divisors contribute an even number to the p-torsion dimension; the divisible Selmer part contributes its corank.
For r=0 or 1, nonnegativity in r=corank+2s forces s=0 and corank=r. This also shows the p∞ Selmer group is respectively zero or a divisible line.
acceptance: A finite cyclic group of order p² has square order but cannot have a perfect alternating pairing; square order alone is not the needed argument.
For a divisible line plus a paired finite part with dim M[p]=1, dim Sel_p=3 and corank=1; equality of dimension and corank is not asserted in higher dimension.

sources.match: Finite Selmer dimension gives the same low-rank converse; the coefficient identification requires the paired-primary structure to finish the corank argument.
Alternation is perfect after quotienting by the divisible kernel and yields paired finite primary factors.

nodes.title: Auxiliary Heegner fields selected from Selmer parity
nodes.statement: Under EisensteinConverseData, if corank Sel_{p∞}(E/ℚ)=r∈{0,1}, infinitely many K satisfy the displayed Heegner/split/discriminant conditions and analyticRank(E^K/ℚ)=1−r. In the r=1 case this means L(E^K,1)≠0; in the r=0 case it means a simple central zero of the twist. No analytic-rank assumption on E enters the choice.
hypotheses: E/ℚ is a Weierstrass curve with IsElliptic, conductor N; p is prime, p>2 and p∤N; ι:E→E′ is a rational cyclic isogeny of degree p. Its actual kernel character φ:G_ℚ→𝔽_pˣ satisfies φ|G_p∉{1,ω}, with ω the mod-p cyclotomic character. The residual quotient character is ψ=ωφ⁻¹.
The rational Selmer corank is r=0 or r=1.
proofSteps: BSD.7a supplies ordinarity. Apply the modular parity theorem to the weight-two realization, using the rational newform bridge and elliptic Kummer comparison: w(E)=(−1)^r.
Apply the value branch of BSD.2/bfh-nonvanishing for w(E)=−1, and its derivative branch for w(E)=+1. In the finite splitting set include every prime dividing N and both 2 and p.

The sign of the negative discriminant is correct in each branch; splitting at 2 makes it odd. Infinitude excludes D=−3,−4. Splitting at every level prime gives (D,N)=1 and the classical Heegner hypothesis.
acceptance: The r=0 branch uses a simple-zero twist and the r=1 branch a nonzero-value twist.
Every level prime is split. Skinner’s residual nonsplit-prime auxiliary field is a different input and cannot be substituted here.

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.2.1, pp. 574–575, conditions (a)–(d) and (d′)
sources.match: Parity determines which of the two complementary nonvanishing branches supplies K.

nodes.title: The selected field has Selmer corank one
nodes.statement: For E,p,r and any K selected in EC.1/auxiliary-fields, corank_ℤp Sel_{p∞}(E/K)=1 and E(K)[p]=0. Thus the precise additional (Sel) hypothesis of CGLS Corollary 4.2.3 is satisfied before the Heegner main conjecture is applied.
hypotheses: E/ℚ is a Weierstrass curve with IsElliptic, conductor N; p is prime, p>2 and p∤N; ι:E→E′ is a rational cyclic isogeny of degree p. Its actual kernel character φ:G_ℚ→𝔽_pˣ satisfies φ|G_p∉{1,ω}, with ω the mod-p cyclotomic character. The residual quotient character is ψ=ωφ⁻¹.
K/ℚ is imaginary quadratic with odd fundamental discriminant D<−4, every prime dividing N splits in K, and p splits as v v̄. No class-number restriction is imposed.
corank Sel_{p∞}(E/ℚ)=r∈{0,1} and analyticRank(E^K)=1−r.
proofSteps: Apply the forward rank-at-most-one theorem only to E^K, whose analytic rank is already known. It gives its Mordell–Weil rank 1−r and finite Sha, hence that Selmer corank.
Use the odd-primary quadratic Selmer decomposition to add the two coranks: r+(1−r)=1.
Because p splits in K, its completions are ℚ_p. The imported local character exclusion kills local p-torsion and therefore E(K)[p].
acceptance: Full Sha finiteness for E is not an input. The forward theorem is used on the twist at this point.

sources.match: The complementary twist and quadratic decomposition establish (Sel) without assuming the desired conclusion for E.

nodes.title: Corank-one control at the augmentation prime
nodes.statement: Under EisensteinConverseData and the Heegner conditions, suppose corank Sel_{p∞}(E/K)=1. Write Λ=ℤ_p⟦Γ⟧, P₀=(γ−1), M_E=T_pE⊗Λ∨ with inverse tautological action, T=M_E∨(1), S=H¹_FΛ(K,T), and X=H¹_FΛ(K,M_E)∨ in CGLS’s ordinary, self-dual convention. The Pontryagin-dual discrete control map has finite kernel and cokernel, so dim_ℚp((X/P₀X)⊗ℚ_p)=1. Together with the supplied rank-one pseudo-isomorphism X∼Λ⊕M⊕M, this gives length_(Λ_P₀)(X_tors,P₀)=0 and v_P₀(char X_tors)=0. Moreover the specialization S/P₀S→H¹_f(K,V_pE) is injective after inverting p.
hypotheses: E/ℚ is a Weierstrass curve with IsElliptic, conductor N; p is prime, p>2 and p∤N; ι:E→E′ is a rational cyclic isogeny of degree p. Its actual kernel character φ:G_ℚ→𝔽_pˣ satisfies φ|G_p∉{1,ω}, with ω the mod-p cyclotomic character. The residual quotient character is ψ=ωφ⁻¹.
K/ℚ is imaginary quadratic with odd fundamental discriminant D<−4, every prime dividing N splits in K, and p splits as v v̄. No class-number restriction is imposed.
Use the exact ordinary local conditions and contragredient action in CGLS §3.4, not the torsion Greenberg dual X_E. Corank Sel_{p∞}(E/K)=1.
proofSteps: Apply SI’s restriction-control diagram to the actual global and local images. The prime-to-p quotient characters stay nontrivial over a pro-p tower, killing the relevant p-adic invariant terms. At v|p use both nontrivial residual factors. Away from p retain the finite local Kummer/Tamagawa and localization-image errors; prove they have ℤ_p-corank zero, rather than assuming localization surjective.

Dualize the resulting finite-kernel/cokernel control and tensor ℚ_p. Localize the supplied pseudo-isomorphism at P₀: pseudo-null errors disappear and Λ_P₀ is a DVR. A nonzero finite-length torsion summand has a nonzero residue quotient, whereas the free rank-one summand already accounts for the entire one-dimensional quotient.

For compact specialization, the global coefficient exact sequence gives the kernel as (γ−1) times the same ordinary compact Selmer module after rationalization. Check saturation of the local conditions using the same local diagrams. The derived-control H²/Tor term can contribute to the cokernel and is retained; no surjectivity is claimed.
acceptance: X denotes the rank-one ordinary dual throughout; replacing it by the Λ-torsion X_E changes the argument.
For Λ⊕Λ/P₀ the rational coinvariant dimension is 2, so corank one excludes this example.
Neither γ−1 nor P₀ is inverted. Finite p-power errors disappear after inverting p, which leaves P₀ available.

sources.locator: §3.4, Corollary 3.4.2 and proof, p. 566; Theorem 5.2.1 proof, p. 574
sources.match: Corank one kills the augmentation-primary ordinary torsion; this is the control input used for nonzero specialization.

nodes.title: The bottom Heegner class and its normalization
nodes.statement: Let κ∞ be the stabilized Heegner class used in CGLS Corollary 4.2.3, P_K=Tr_(K[1]/K)π(x₁), and α the p-adic unit root of X²−a_pX+p. Its bottom specialization is κ₀=u_K⁻¹(1−α⁻¹)²·Kummer(P_K) in H¹(K,V_pE), where u_K=#O_Kˣ/2=1 for D<−4. For the Howard-normalized class κ₁^Hg, pr_K(κ₁^Hg)=u_K α²(β−1)² κ₀ with β=pα⁻¹. The two tower classes generate the same Λ-line. Under the local exclusion both displayed scalar factors are p-adic units.
hypotheses: E/ℚ is a Weierstrass curve with IsElliptic, conductor N; p is prime, p>2 and p∤N; ι:E→E′ is a rational cyclic isogeny of degree p. Its actual kernel character φ:G_ℚ→𝔽_pˣ satisfies φ|G_p∉{1,ω}, with ω the mod-p cyclotomic character. The residual quotient character is ψ=ωφ⁻¹.
K/ℚ is imaginary quadratic with odd fundamental discriminant D<−4, every prime dividing N splits in K, and p splits as v v̄. No class-number restriction is imposed.
Use the same modular parametrization and ring-class trace in the class and the complex Gross–Zagier formula.
proofSteps: Import the actual norm-compatible Heegner family and its Kummer/Shapiro map from HE.8. At split p take the trace of (1−α⁻¹σ_v)(1−α⁻¹σ_v̄)P[1]/u_K; the Artin actions disappear after the full ring-class trace.
Use CGLS Remark 4.1.3, equations (4.4)–(4.5), to compare the Howard and stabilized normalizations. Keep α, β and u_K explicit.

Ordinarity and the two excluded residual factors imply a_p≠1 modulo p, hence α−1 is a unit; β is divisible by p and β−1 is a unit. The same comparison handles p dividing the ring-class number without division by that number.
acceptance: Nonzero tower class alone does not imply nonzero bottom class; EC.2/augmentation-control and the equality are still required.
The normalization uses (1−α⁻¹)² after the full trace; it is not the finite group-ring initial factor before trace.

sources.match: The exact norm-compatible stabilization and comparison identify the actual bottom Kummer class.

nodes.title: The Heegner point is non-torsion from corank one
nodes.statement: Under EisensteinConverseData and the Heegner conditions, corank Sel_{p∞}(E/K)=1 implies that the specified classical trace point P_K has infinite order. In particular ord_(s=1)L(E/K,s)=1.
hypotheses: E/ℚ is a Weierstrass curve with IsElliptic, conductor N; p is prime, p>2 and p∤N; ι:E→E′ is a rational cyclic isogeny of degree p. Its actual kernel character φ:G_ℚ→𝔽_pˣ satisfies φ|G_p∉{1,ω}, with ω the mod-p cyclotomic character. The residual quotient character is ψ=ωφ⁻¹.
K/ℚ is imaginary quadratic with odd fundamental discriminant D<−4, every prime dividing N splits in K, and p splits as v v̄. No class-number restriction is imposed.
The Heegner point, ordinary modules and stabilized class have the normalization fixed in EC.2/heegner-specialization-factor.
proofSteps: Apply the parent’s CGLS prototype equality, including its explicit (Sel) hypothesis, to obtain char(X_tors)=char(S/Λκ∞)² in Λ[1/p], with S and X of Λ-rank one.
EC.2/augmentation-control gives valuation zero on the left. At P₀ this equality forces S_P₀=Λ_P₀ κ∞. In particular κ∞ has nonzero image in (S/P₀S)⊗ℚ_p.

Use the injective compact specialization map and the exact bottom factor to obtain Kummer(P_K)≠0, hence P_K is non-torsion. Use the existing canonical-height nonnegativity and zero-iff-torsion statements; number-field Northcott and the finite-fiber x-coordinate comparison discharge their finiteness hypothesis. Import GZ.0’s pinned/Poincaré height normalization, which changes this height only by explicit positive factors. Apply the classical X₀(N) Gross–Zagier formula with all level primes split and nonzero normalization to get L′(E/K,1)≠0. Its root number is −1, so the order is exactly one.
acceptance: A divisibility after inverting γ−1 cannot yield this conclusion. The equality is used at P₀ before specialization.
Do not use the rank-one BSD control formula whose hypotheses already include Mordell–Weil rank one and finite Sha.

sources.match: The main-conjecture equality at augmentation proves nonzero classical Heegner specialization and then a simple analytic zero.

nodes.title: The Eisenstein-prime p-converse
nodes.statement: Under EisensteinConverseData, for each r∈{0,1}, corank_ℤp Sel_{p∞}(E/ℚ)=r implies analyticRank(E)=r. Equivalently the shared CMRankZeroConverse:C.0/p-converse-property holds for r=0 and r=1 under these hypotheses. The analytic rank is the order of the actual arithmetic L-function at 1.
hypotheses: E/ℚ is a Weierstrass curve with IsElliptic, conductor N; p is prime, p>2 and p∤N; ι:E→E′ is a rational cyclic isogeny of degree p. Its actual kernel character φ:G_ℚ→𝔽_pˣ satisfies φ|G_p∉{1,ω}, with ω the mod-p cyclotomic character. The residual quotient character is ψ=ωφ⁻¹.
r is a natural number equal to 0 or 1.
proofSteps: Choose K by EC.1/auxiliary-fields and establish its Selmer corank one by EC.1/selmer-corank-over-k.
Apply EC.2/heegner-point-nontorsion to obtain analyticRank(E/K)=1.
Use the parent’s quadratic L-factorization and addition of central analytic orders: 1=analyticRank(E)+analyticRank(E^K). Subtract the already known complementary twist order 1−r.
acceptance: For r=0 the conclusion is L(E,1)≠0; for r=1 it is a simple zero.
There is no squarefree-conductor, residual irreducibility, large-p or extra global parity assumption on the kernel character.

sources.match: The two complementary-twist choices prove both low-corank converses.

nodes.title: Arithmetic rank equality and finite Sha
nodes.statement: Under EisensteinConverseData and corank Sel_{p∞}(E/ℚ)=r∈{0,1}, rank_ℤ E(ℚ)=analyticRank(E)=r and Sha(E/ℚ) is finite as a whole group. This conclusion is stronger than finiteness of only Sha[p∞], but it asserts no BSD leading-coefficient or p-valuation identity.
hypotheses: E/ℚ is a Weierstrass curve with IsElliptic, conductor N; p is prime, p>2 and p∤N; ι:E→E′ is a rational cyclic isogeny of degree p. Its actual kernel character φ:G_ℚ→𝔽_pˣ satisfies φ|G_p∉{1,ω}, with ω the mod-p cyclotomic character. The residual quotient character is ψ=ωφ⁻¹.
corank Sel_{p∞}(E/ℚ)=r∈{0,1}.
proofSteps: First apply the p-converse to establish analytic rank r.
Apply the existing forward analytic-rank-at-most-one theorem over ℚ. Its separate outputs give the rank and full Sha finiteness.
acceptance: Sha finiteness is an output reached after the analytic converse. It is never an assumption on E.

sources.match: The forward Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin theorem supplies the arithmetic consequences of the converse.

nodes.title: The finite-Selmer converse
nodes.statement: Under EisensteinConverseData, if dim_𝔽p Sel_p(E/ℚ)=r∈{0,1}, then analyticRank(E)=rank_ℤ E(ℚ)=r and Sha(E/ℚ) is finite.
hypotheses: E/ℚ is a Weierstrass curve with IsElliptic, conductor N; p is prime, p>2 and p∤N; ι:E→E′ is a rational cyclic isogeny of degree p. Its actual kernel character φ:G_ℚ→𝔽_pˣ satisfies φ|G_p∉{1,ω}, with ω the mod-p cyclotomic character. The residual quotient character is ψ=ωφ⁻¹.
The finite-level Selmer group uses the Kummer local conditions, not a chosen abstract F_p-vector space.
proofSteps: Use EC.0/small-selmer-corank, including the Cassels–Tate modulo-divisible pairing, to obtain the correct p∞ corank.
Apply EC.3/p-converse and EC.3/rank-and-sha.
acceptance: A one-dimensional Sel_p does not give corank one by the coefficient identification alone; the paired finite-part argument is essential.
The theorem includes p=3. It does not import Skinner’s p≥5, irreducible residual localization criterion.

sources.match: The low-dimensional finite-Selmer hypothesis gives the same complete conclusion.

nodes.title: The admissible three-isogeny twist family
nodes.statement: Fix an actual rational cyclic 3-isogeny ι:E→E′ with kernel character φ. Inside the existing unweighted family ℚˣ/ℚˣ² set A₃(E,ι)={d : E^d has good reduction at 3 and (φχ_d)|G₃∉{1,ω}}. Here χ_d is the quadratic character of ℚ(√d), and the twisted isogeny has kernel character φχ_d. Count each squareclass once through its unique nonzero signed squarefree integer representative, ordered by |d|. A₃ is determined solely by its allowed local squareclasses at 3.
hypotheses: E/ℚ is elliptic and ι is an actual degree-3 isogeny. No existence of a good-at-3 twist is built into the definition.
proofSteps: Pull back the good-reduction and local-character conditions along localization ℚˣ/ℚˣ²→ℚ₃ˣ/ℚ₃ˣ². Use upstream quadratic twisting and the existing squareclass-height family.
Good reduction and the local kernel character depend only on the local isogeny diagram, so the subset is independent of representatives.
acceptance: The family includes good reduction as well as the character exclusion. A rational 3-isogeny alone does not imply it is nonempty.

sources.match: The converse is applied only on twists satisfying its good-prime and local-character hypotheses.
The denominator is unweighted squareclasses ordered by the norm product of primes with odd valuation, which over ℚ is the absolute squarefree representative.

uses.how: Keep the same local conditions on the family to which the converse is applied.
Distinguish a positive local family from an empty one and compute the actual denominator.

tests.name: TauCeti.RankZeroOneBSDPartII.admissibleTwists_nontrivial_unramified

nodes.title: Positive Selmer-ratio strata within the admissible family
nodes.statement: Suppose E/ℚ has a rational 3-isogeny and at least one quadratic twist with good reduction at 3. For the fixed isogeny write T_m={d:c(ι^d)=3^m} using the signed convention. Then A₃∩T₀ and A₃∩(T₁∪T₋₁) each contain a nonempty finite-local-condition family and have positive density among all signed squarefree parameters ordered by |d|.
hypotheses: ι:E→E′ is a rational cyclic 3-isogeny. There exists d₀ with E^d₀ good at 3. No explicit numerical lower density independent of E is asserted.
proofSteps: At 3 fix a local squareclass d₀u for which the twist is good ordinary and the kernel character is allowed: among the two unramified twists of a good model exactly one avoids both 1 and ω. This also kills local 3-torsion on E and E′.

Use the existing local Selmer-ratio formula: at 3 the good-model ratio is 1 or 3, depending on whether the kernel lies in the formal group. It stays fixed on this chosen local class. At each bad prime ℓ≠3 choose a local twist with c_ℓ=1 by BKLOS Proposition 10.7; outside 3N every twist has ratio 1.

At the real place the two signs give ratios 1 and 1/3. Hence the two choices give global ratios (1,1/3) or (3,1), providing both the zero and an odd signed stratum while preserving the chosen 3-adic class.

Weak approximation makes each compatible finite local prescription nonempty. Apply the rational squarefree local-density count with its nonuniform local squareclass masses to obtain positive density. The argument is directly on E’s family; translating by d₀ is not assumed to preserve height.
acceptance: The local class at 3 is fixed before applying statistics, and cannot be changed independently after selecting a Selmer-rank set.
If the finite-place ratio is 1, the odd stratum obtained is T₋₁; if it is 3, it is T₁. Both are covered by the absolute-ratio-one bound.

sources.locator: Proposition 10.1, p. 14; Theorem 10.5, pp. 15–16; Proposition 10.7, p. 17; §11 proof of Theorem 2.6, p. 18
sources.match: Local ratios and the real sign produce nonempty zero and odd strata. The present application keeps an admissible good-reduction local class at 3 fixed.
Restricting the statistical input to the local family is the additional compatibility check required by the converse.

nodes.title: Analytic-rank bounds in prescribed admissible families
nodes.statement: Let Σ⊂A₃ be a nonempty family defined by finitely many local conditions. Put Σ₀=Σ∩T₀ and Σ₁=Σ∩(T₁∪T₋₁). For either nonempty stratum, the lower proportion within Σ₀ of twists with analytic rank and Mordell–Weil rank 0 and finite Sha is at least 1/2, and the lower proportion within Σ₁ with both ranks 1 and finite Sha is at least 5/6. Relative to all signed squarefree twists these give lower bounds (1/2)μ(Σ₀) and (5/6)μ(Σ₁), with μ the same height density.
hypotheses: ι:E→E′ is a rational cyclic 3-isogeny. The finite local prescriptions defining Σ are globally compatible. Each displayed conditional proportion is asserted only when its denominator stratum is nonempty.
proofSteps: Import ST.5’s restricted-family 3-Selmer-rank-zero and rank-one bounds, with their signed/absolute ratio convention.
For d∈A₃ the local exclusion gives E^d(ℚ)[3]=0, so the supplier’s adjusted 3-Selmer rank equals the actual F₃ dimension. Apply EC.3/mod-p-converse to the zero- and one-dimensional subsets.

Use the existing relative-density tower theorem. The stratum densities exist by finite local conditions; multiplication by their fixed density yields the absolute lower bounds, without asserting existence of an analytic-rank limiting density.
acceptance: Keep the Σ₀ and Σ₁ denominators, and multiply by their actual densities before reporting percentages among all twists.
These are lower proportions, not exact Goldfeld densities or percentages for the original unrestricted ratio strata.

sources.match: The average/parity argument gives the 1/2 and 5/6 bounds on finite local subfamilies.
The finite-Selmer converse converts the correctly restricted statistical subsets to analytic-rank subsets.

nodes.title: Positive proportions of rank-zero and rank-one twists
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ admit a rational cyclic 3-isogeny and at least one quadratic twist with good reduction at 3. Among the distinct nonzero signed squarefree integers d ordered by |d|, a positive lower proportion have rank E^d(ℚ)=analyticRank(E^d)=0 and finite Sha(E^d/ℚ), and a positive lower proportion have the analogous rank-one conclusion.
hypotheses: Existence of a good-at-3 twist is an explicit hypothesis. The family is the unweighted squareclass family, not discriminants ordered by their absolute value or minimal curves ordered by naive height.
proofSteps: Use EC.4/admissible-ratio-strata to find positive-density finite-local-condition families in the two relevant admissible strata.
Apply EC.4/relative-proportion-bounds and multiply their positive densities by 1/2 or 5/6. These products are strictly positive.
acceptance: No analytic-rank conclusion is claimed for the complement of A₃ by this argument. No result about density one-half for either rank is asserted.

sources.locator: Corollary 5.2.3, p. 575, with the good-at-3 scope made explicit
sources.match: The restricted method proves positive proportions under the good-twist hypothesis; the larger printed scope is recorded in sourceIssues.
Positive finite-local-condition Selmer strata combine with the converse.

nodes.title: The nineteen-a3 Weierstrass model
nodes.statement: Define nineteenA3:WeierstrassCurve ℚ by (a₁,a₂,a₃,a₄,a₆)=(0,1,1,1,0), so its equation is y²+y=x³+x²+x. This is only a concrete diagnostic model on the existing carrier; it introduces no database label, elliptic-curve type or new twist operation.
hypotheses: The model is over ℚ. Its nonzero discriminant is a theorem, not a data placeholder.
proofSteps: Fill the five existing coefficient fields and compute with the existing invariant formulas.
acceptance: The coefficient a₂ is 1 and a₃ is 1. Replacing this by a short Weierstrass equation changes both the model and the tests.

nodes.title: The actual local family for nineteen-a3
nodes.statement: For nineteenA3 with the cyclic isogeny generated by P=(0,0), the admissible signed squarefree parameters are exactly d≡2 modulo 3. Their density among all signed squarefree d ordered by |d| is 3/8. In particular a rank-one analytic subset obtained solely by EC.3/mod-p-converse at p=3 inside this family has upper density at most 3/8 in the full family; the number 41.6% cannot be obtained by that restricted conversion.
hypotheses: Use the exact model, its actual rational kernel P, and signed squarefree parameters. This statement puts no upper bound on the actual full rank-one twist set.
proofSteps: Compute Δ=−19, hence good reduction at 3. Count six points on E(F₃), giving a₃=−2 and ordinary reduction; the tangent calculation certifies P has order3, so φ is trivial.

The two unit squareclasses at 3 preserve good reduction, but only the nonsquare unit changes the local kernel character to the allowed nontrivial unramified one. The ramified squareclasses have bad reduction. Thus membership is precisely 3∤d and d mod3=2.

Apply the existing squarefree coprime-residue count with modulus3 separately to positive and negative parameters. The count of 3∤d is 3/4 of all squarefree parameters, and each unit residue accounts for half of it: density 3/8.

Any subset of this admissible family has upper density at most 3/8. For valid analytic lower bounds use the intersections with T₀ and T₁∪T₋₁ from EC.4; no unrestricted numerical percentages are transferred.
acceptance: The density is 3/8 in signed squarefree parameters, not 1/2 from uniform weighting of the two unramified local classes.
P=(0,0) is a point distinct from the group identity at infinity.
The diagnostic rejects the proposed argument for the published percentages; it does not disprove those percentages for the full twist family.

sources.match: Its explicit example requires an admissible-family denominator before applying the converse.

nodes.title: A three-isogeny does not guarantee a good-at-three twist
nodes.statement: The rational Weierstrass curve W:y²+xy+3y=x³ has a rational cyclic 3-isogeny, but no quadratic twist has good reduction at3. Indeed (0,0) has order3, Δ(W)=−2160, c₄(W)=−71, and j(W)=357911/2160 has 3-adic valuation−3. Every quadratic twist has the same j; good reduction would make j integral. Thus A₃(W,ι)=∅.
hypotheses: W has coefficients (1,0,3,0,0) over ℚ and ι is the isogeny with kernel generated by (0,0).
proofSteps: The tangent at (0,0) is y=0; its intersection with the cubic has multiplicity3, proving the nonidentity point has order3. Use upstream quotient-by-stable-kernel to obtain the actual isogeny.
Compute the invariant formulas and v₃(j)=−3. Use existing twist invariance of j and the local integral-j consequence of good reduction to exclude every twist.

Apply the definition of A₃. This is a counterexample to the claim that the converse method’s good-reduction hypotheses can always be reached by quadratic twisting, not to the full printed analytic density conclusion by other methods.
acceptance: Twisting can change the residual kernel character, but it cannot change j or make a negative valuation integral.

Export BKLOS local calculations: c∞ is1 or1/3 with both signs attainable; for ℓ≠3 some local twist has cℓ=1 and all twists have cℓ=1 away from3N; at good ordinary3 the ratio is1 or3 by the connected/étale kernel. In particular a fixed unit nonsquare class at3 has mass3/8 among all signed squarefree parameters. No general-number-field denominator theorem is assumed.

review.reason: Confirmed at CGLS Corollary 5.2.3, p.575, and arXiv v2 p.32. The proof invokes a converse whose standing hypothesis is good reduction at p (published pp.518–519). The rational flex on y²+xy+3y=x³ supplies a 3-isogeny, while its twist-invariant j has v₃=−3. Thus character twisting alone cannot put every family inside that converse. This confirms a proof gap, not falsity of the qualitative density theorem.
